name: GO Classes CS Test Series 2025 | Compiler Design | Topic Wise Test 3

question.text:
A node $p$ in a control flow graph(CFG) $\text{N}$ dominates a node $q$ if every path from the entry node to $q$ goes through $p$. We say that node $p$ is a dominator of node $q.$
The dominator set of node $q,\; \text{DOM(}q),$ is formed by all nodes that dominate $q.$ By definition, each node dominates itself, therefore, $\mathrm{q} \in \operatorname{DOM}(\mathrm{q})$

  • $\mathrm{p}$ dominates $\mathrm{q}$, written $\mathrm{p} \leq \mathrm{q}$, i.e. $\mathrm{p} \in \operatorname{DOM}(\mathrm{q})$.
  • $\mathrm{p}$ properly (strictly) dominates $\mathrm{q}$, written $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{q}$ if $\mathrm{p} \leq \mathrm{q}$ and $\mathrm{p} \neq \mathrm{q}$.
  • $\mathrm{p}$ immediately (or directly) dominates $\mathrm{q}$, if $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{q}$ and there is no node $t$ such that $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{t}<\mathrm{q}$.

We say $p$ is the immediate dominator of $q$ and write $p=\operatorname{IDOM}(q)$

Consider the following basic block, in which all variables are integers.

a := b + c
z := a * a
x := 0
y := a
w := a * a
u := 3
v := u + w

Assume that the only variables that are live at the exit of this block are $\textsf{v}$ and $\textsf{z}.$
Consider the following transformation of the given basic block after applying a particular optimization.

a := b + c
z := a * a
w := a * a
u := 3
v := u + w

Which of the following best describes the optimization that has been performed?

  1. algebraic simplification
  2. common sub-expression elimination
  3. copy propagation
  4. dead code elimination

Which of the following statements regarding SSA form (Static Single Assignment form) of an intermediate representation is False?

  1. If a program is in SSA form, then use of a variable is reached by exactly one definition of that variable.
  2. Flow of control in SSA form remains the same as in the non-SSA form.
  3. Since every variable has exactly one definition in the program text, so there are no loops in SSA form
  4. Some compiler optimizations perform better on SSA forms.
